source: Bell et al. (2021), MNRAS 504, 3316, 'A comprehensive reanalysis of Spitzer's 4.5 um phase curves, and the phase variations of the ultra-hot Jupiters MASCARA-1b and KELT-16b' (doi:10.1093/mnras/stab1027; arXiv:2010.00687). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve of HAT-P-7b, program 60021, first published by Wong et al. (2016) and reanalysed here. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: the table of preferred SPCA model parameters (tab:preferred), row HAT-P-7b, detector model BLISS. The preferred fit is first order (the caption of its figure names the mode BLISS_v1), so the printed semi-amplitude and offset are the whole phase variation (section 4.1: semi-amplitude sqrt(C1^2 + D1^2), offset east -arctan2(D1, C1)). The paper notes that its models prefer an unusually flat phase curve for HAT-P-7b compared with Wong et al. (2016), that the offset becomes poorly defined as the amplitude approaches zero, and that the offset scatters between its detector models by more than the fitted uncertainty.

model.equation: F_p = F_day [1 + C1 (cos psi - 1) + D1 sin psi], psi counted from mid-eclipse (section 4.1), printed as its semi-amplitude and the offset east of its maximum.
